title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
layout_note: Two columns: (a) the locked Stable Diffusion U-Net drawn as a top-to-bottom stack of encoder, middle and decoder blocks, and (b) ControlNet as a trainable copy of the encoder half in a dashed frame on the right, feeding back through zero convolutions into the decoder blocks.
grouping: Column (b) is enclosed in a dotted teal frame; column (a) is unframed; the two are captioned (a) Stable Diffusion and (b) ControlNet under each column.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with grey outlines; locked blocks light grey with a padlock icon; trainable copies light teal with teal outlines; zero convolutions as white pill shapes; block widths taper with resolution (64x64 wide, 8x8 narrow); no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The proposed copy is the only teal-filled region, in its own dotted frame, with teal arrows for all its connections; the original network is greyed and padlocked to say it is frozen.
lesson: Mark frozen versus trained parts with fill plus a padlock icon (grey + lock vs. accent-coloured 'trainable copy'), and give the added side network its own dashed frame and line colour so its every connection is traceable.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue ICCV 2023 (not verified in this session). Figure 2 is the single-block version of the same idea (before/after); Figure 3 chosen as the full architecture.

arrangement.units: two columns: (a) the locked Stable Diffusion block stack, unframed; (b) the ControlNet copy in a dotted teal frame
arrangement.inputs_as: math labels: Prompt c_t and Time t over their encoders, Input z_t, and Condition c_f above the ControlNet frame
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn; the output epsilon_theta(z_t, t, c_t, c_f) is written under column (a)
arrangement.shared: the prompt and time embeddings are routed into both columns by one grey bus line labelled Prompt&Time

insights.structure: Two vertical stacks side by side: nine Stable Diffusion blocks on the left, and on the right a dotted teal frame holding the trainable encoder copies with a column of zero-convolution pills below them aligned to the decoder blocks they feed.
insights.data: No data is pictured; inputs and the output are math labels (c_t, t, z_t, c_f, epsilon_theta), and each block carries its feature resolution (64x64 ... 8x8) with x3 repeat counts beside it.
insights.emphasis: Teal fill, teal outlines and teal arrows belong only to ControlNet, while every original block is grey with a padlock, so frozen vs. trainable reads without a legend.
insights.flow: Both columns read top to bottom; the teal side lines then run down the right edge and turn left into each decoder block through a zero convolution, one line per resolution.
insights.avoid: The skip lines inside column (a) and the many thin parallel grey/teal verticals with x3 labels make the space between the columns busy; thin parallel lines with repeated labels are hard to follow.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
